turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_max_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_max_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data show a clear dominance of `solution_aged` + `wrought` for the highest measured yield strengths (multiple examples 648–713 MPa). Other heat-treatment/route combinations top out substantially lower (quench-temper wrought \(\approx\) 611 MPa, solution-aged AM \(\approx\) 638 MPa, everything else \(\lt\) 550 MPa). Consequently only the nine pool members that are themselves `solution_aged` + `wrought` were examined in detail.

Nearest-neighbor matching on composition + aging temperature then ranks those nine:

- c008 is almost identical to the 648 MPa training row (C, Si, Mo, V, aging temperature all within a few percent) \(\to\) \(\approx\) 650 MPa.
- c038 matches the 613 MPa row on C, Ni, Nb, aging temperature and solutionizing temperature \(\to\) \(\approx\) 610 MPa.
- c015 matches the 594 MPa row on C, Si, Cr, Ni, Al, Cu and aging temperature \(\to\) \(\approx\) 590 MPa.
- c072 shares the Co–Mo–Ni–V signature of the 698 MPa row (aging temperature only 50 °C higher) \(\to\) \(\approx\) 570 MPa.
- c021 shares the low-C, Cr–Ni–Nb–Ti signature of several 550–600 MPa rows \(\to\) \(\approx\) 560 MPa.

The remaining four `solution_aged` + `wrought` candidates have either far lower aging temperatures or compositions whose nearest training analogues sit at 500–530 MPa and are therefore discarded.

Final: c008, c038, c015, c072, c021
